fact: PM-KISAN provides Rs. 6000 per year to eligible farmer families, paid in three equal installments of Rs. 2000 each every four months (April-July, August-November, December-March).
A PM-KISAN beneficiary family is defined as husband, wife and minor children who own cultivable land as per land records of the concerned State/UT.

Institutional land holders, current or former constitutional post holders/ministers/legislators, serving or retired government employees (except Group D/Class IV staff), pensioners with monthly pension of Rs. 10,000 or more, income tax payers, registered professionals (doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, architects), and NRIs are excluded from PM-KISAN.

PM-KISAN registration requires an Aadhaar number (or Aadhaar enrolment number plus another ID like Voter ID), bank account number with IFSC code, and land records; Assam, Meghalaya and Jammu & Kashmir were exempted from the Aadhaar requirement till 31.3.2021.

The cut-off date for determining PM-KISAN beneficiary eligibility was 01.02.2019, with no changes considered thereafter for 5 years, except when ownership transfer happens due to the landowner's death.

PM-KISAN funds are transferred directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) through the PFMS portal, after State/UT governments upload and e-sign verified farmer lists on the PM-KISAN Portal at pmkisan.gov.in.

PM-JAY provides cashless health cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 per eligible family per year for listed secondary and tertiary care, on a family floater basis with no cap on family size or age, and pre-existing diseases covered from day one.
PM-JAY beneficiaries are persons covered under specific categories of the SECC-2011 database of the Government of India; there is no income criterion for beneficiaries already listed under SECC-2011.
Eligibility documents for Ayushman Bharat include a PM/CM entitlement letter, ration card, or Aadhaar card for identification.

PM-JAY covers 874 treatment packages and 1592 procedures, including consultation, pre-hospitalization, medicines, diagnostics, implants, accommodation, food, and 15 days of post-hospitalization follow-up; OPD services are not covered.
Beneficiaries can get an Ayushman card at Ayushman Kiosks in empanelled hospitals or at Common Service Centres (CSC), and can check their eligibility online at mera.pmjay.gov.in.
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY has no application deadline; it is an ongoing scheme with rolling enrolment for eligible SECC-2011 families.

A PMAY-Urban beneficiary is defined as a family of husband, wife and unmarried children who do not own a pucca house anywhere in India; EWS beneficiaries are eligible under all four scheme verticals, while LIG/MIG beneficiaries are eligible only under the Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS).

PMAY-Urban's Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) gives an interest subsidy of up to Rs. 2.67 lakh per house: 6.5% on loans up to Rs. 6 lakh for EWS/LIG, 4% on loans up to Rs. 9 lakh for MIG-I, and 3% on loans up to Rs. 12 lakh for MIG-II.
PMAY-Urban income categories are: EWS up to Rs. 3 lakh/year, LIG Rs. 3-6 lakh/year, MIG-I Rs. 6-12 lakh/year, and MIG-II Rs. 12-18 lakh/year.
CLSS carpet area limits are up to 30 sq.m for EWS, 60 sq.m for LIG, 160 sq.m for MIG-I, and 200 sq.m for MIG-II; exceeding these limits makes a beneficiary ineligible for the subsidy.

The PMAY-Urban interest subsidy is credited upfront to the beneficiary's loan account by the Primary Lending Institution, reducing the principal loan amount and the EMI; NHB, HUDCO and SBI are the Central Nodal Agencies that channel the subsidy to lenders.
PMAY-Urban was launched on 25 June 2015 with an original target of housing for all eligible urban households by 2022.

Post-Matric Scholarship maintenance allowance ranges from Rs. 1200/month (hostellers) or Rs. 550/month (day scholars) for Group I courses down to Rs. 380/month (hostellers) or Rs. 230/month (day scholars) for Group IV courses, plus reimbursement of compulsory non-refundable fees.

Post-Matric Scholarship is open to Scheduled Caste students studying post-matriculation or post-secondary courses whose parents'/guardians' income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 2,50,000 per year.

An application requires the prescribed application form, a passport-size photograph, attested copies of certificates, an original caste certificate signed by a Revenue Officer not below Tehsildar rank, and an income declaration or certificate.
States announce the scheme and invite applications in May-June each year; applicants must submit the completed application before the last date prescribed by their State/UT.

The scheme is implemented by State Governments/UT Administrations with 100% central assistance from the Government of India; scholarship money is paid into the student's post office or bank account, not in cash.
